content.text: Carmen rejects social ambition and sectarian religion, embracing love, spiritual truth, and the Christ-principle. She meets Father Waite at the Beaubien mansion, where she rebukes Monsignor Lafelle. After Hawley-Crowles’s ruin and suicide, Carmen and the Beaubien move to a modest bungalow. There, Father Waite forms a study group, and Carmen enters the University. In Doctor Morton’s laboratory, she argues that disease and death arise from false material beliefs. Carmen and Hitt help Haynerd transform the Express into a reform newspaper, while she confronts Ames at his mansion and rescues his addicted son Sidney at the Express office. The group studies God, matter, evil, Jesus, and the Bible, concluding that reality is divine Mind and good, while material existence and evil are suppositional errors.
